title: Landscaping CRM Automation
html:
Conversions in spring

A kitchen and bath company scaled to 60 conversions during the spring remodeling surge, the kind of seasonal spike that overloads an office.

Lower cost per lead

A bathroom remodeling company added Dynamic Search Ads to expand reach while reducing cost per lead.

Landscape CRM Software vs CRM Automation Service

A landscape CRM stores contacts and jobs. CRM automation does the follow up, reminders and review requests on top of it. It also ties each lead back to the ad or call that produced it.

Missed-Call Text Back

A homeowner who calls about a patio and reaches voicemail calls the next company on the list. A text back within minutes keeps the lead. Test yours: call your own number after hours, and if no text arrives in 5 minutes, that lead is gone.

  • Tracked call numbers
  • Web form capture
  • Instant text reply
  • Lead source logged

Estimate Follow Up

Bids go quiet after the quote is sent. After three check-ins with no reply, the lead moves to a slower seasonal list.

  • Timed check-in messages
  • Stops on reply
  • Paths by job type
  • Task for your office

Seasonal Reminders

Landscaping demand follows the calendar. Past customers get a spring start-up note, a fall cleanup reminder and a winter planning offer, each timed to your area's first and last frost.

  • Spring start-up note
  • Fall cleanup reminder
  • Winter planning offer
  • Customer list segments

Contract Renewals

Mowing and maintenance contracts renew on a date, and a missed renewal is quiet lost revenue. Reminders go out 60 days, 30 days and 7 days before the end date, and accounts that stay silent are flagged for a call.

  • Three-step reminders
  • End-date tracking
  • Silent account flags
  • Renewal reporting

Review Requests

A short text or email goes out after each finished job with a direct link to your Google profile. Replies that report a problem alert your office the same day, so you can answer before the customer gives up.

  • Post-job request
  • Direct Google link
  • Same-day problem alert
  • Response tracking

How Setup Works

Setup runs in four steps. Timeframes are targets, and your office approves every message before it is sent.

Optimize

Sequences that get no replies are rewritten, and sequences that work are copied to other service types.

Landscaping CRM Software Compared

The right setup depends on how leads reach you and who answers them. This table compares five ways to handle estimate follow up, from an inbox to the tools behind a good CRM for landscaping companies.

Leads from ads often go unanswered unless someone builds the follow up

Is Marketing Automation for Landscaping Companies Right for You?

Automation helps most when leads arrive faster than your office can answer them. It helps less when work comes only from referrals you already manage by phone.

Start now if

  • You run Google or Meta ads and some leads never get a call back.
  • Estimates go out and you rarely check on them.
  • You sell repeat contracts that renew each season.
  • Leads call after hours or while crews are on site.

Wait if

  • Nearly all work comes from a few commercial accounts you already manage by phone.
  • Your crew schedule is full and you are not taking new work.
  • You have no written estimate process yet, so fix that first.
  • Your jobs need a site visit before any price can be given.

FAQs About Landscaping CRM Automation

These are the questions landscaping owners ask before they set up a CRM or automate follow up.

How does a CRM help track landscaping projects?

A CRM keeps each lead, estimate and job in one record with its stage, source and next step. Your office sees which bids are waiting, which jobs are scheduled and which customers are due for seasonal work. Automation then sends the reminders, so nothing depends on memory or sticky notes.

What features should a landscaping CRM have?

Look for lead capture from calls and forms, estimate stages, automatic text and email follow up, seasonal reminders and a simple report by lead source. If you run ads, it should also record which ad produced each lead. Skip features your crews will not use.

What are the benefits of using a landscaping CRM?

A landscaping CRM answers leads faster, shows which estimates are still open and keeps past customers in view for repeat work. It also records which lead sources book jobs, so you can spend ad budget where it pays instead of guessing.

What is the best CRM for landscaping?

The best choice is the one your office will use every day. If you mainly need scheduling and invoices, field service software may be enough. If leads come from ads and calls, add automation that follows up and reports by source.

How much does a landscaping CRM cost?

Software prices vary by company size and features, so check each vendor's current price. Automation setup is a separate cost.
